turns.prompt_text: do they make the color blindness in contact lens version
turns.response_html:
Yes, they do.

Specialized tinted contact lenses, such as those from ChromaGen or ColorMax, use wavelength-filtering technology similar to color-blind glasses. They work by filtering out overlapping light signals to help your brain better distinguish between reds and greens.

Key Things to Know

  • Customization: These are often custom-prescribed and can be worn in both eyes or just one (monocular) to help with color perception without distorting your overall vision too much.
  • Availability: While brands like EnChroma focus on glasses, ChromaGen is the primary FDA-cleared option for color-correcting contact lenses.
  • Not a "Cure": They don't give you "normal" vision, but they can help you pass the Ishihara plate tests (the circles with hidden numbers) and distinguish traffic lights or clothing colors.

Since you find inserting lenses difficult, would you like me to look for color-blind glasses alternatives or find a local eye doctor in Ankeny who fits these specialty lenses?
